title: Research Assistant prompt forbids undeveloped mouse/keyboard and code-write capabilities
description: Research Assistant prompt/runtime surfaces previously exposed negative unavailable-capability language such as forbidding mouse/keyboard control or code writing. The fix moved active prompts into Prompt Pack files, removed the obsolete negative capability bans from active prompt and health/runtime payloads, and keeps real governance boundaries as positive implemented capabilities: MCP/API, approval, Trace and Memory/Audit discipline.
reproduce_command: rg -n "mouse_keyboard_control|code_write|legacy Chinese mouse/keyboard ban phrase|legacy Chinese code-write ban phrase" backend/services/research_assistant prompt_packs/research_assistant/main configs/research_assistant frontend/src/app/research-assistant backend/mcp/modules/research_assistant.py
required_verification: Static scan confirms active root prompt, prompt pack, runtime config, Research Assistant frontend route and MCP module do not contain undeveloped mouse/keyboard or code-write ban phrases.
Backend tests cover enabled prompt-node listing and health payload so negative unavailable-capability metadata is not user-facing.
Health/runtime payload describes implemented capabilities and governance boundaries positively.
Production DDL for prior prompt/runtime schema changes was applied and verified before runtime activation; this closure PR adds no new DDL or dependencies.
closure_requirements: Prompt source and active prompt-node records no longer expose undeveloped mouse/keyboard or code-write bans.
Unavailable capability booleans are not user-facing in health/runtime payloads.
MCP/API approval, traceability and audit boundaries remain enforced.
Tests and static scans cover prompt source, prompt-node listing and runtime capability payloads.
non_goals: Do not implement mouse/keyboard control in this issue.
Do not implement code-writing capability in Research Assistant chat in this issue.
Do not weaken MCP/API approval, traceability, or audit boundaries.
Do not restart production runtime services without explicit approval.
